title: Docs: clarify region selection headers + supported values (benchmark reproduction)
author: Wei Chen
description:
Context: The public “Latency/$” benchmark report includes a “How to replicate” section that references selecting a region via headers when using the OpenAI-compatible API. We’ve had internal review comments that the header name, precedence, and supported values weren’t explicit enough, and a few folks assumed `OpenAI-Organization` or URL host selection did the same thing. This PR clarifies the region selection mechanism in this repo’s docs and aligns examples with the report language.

What changed: (1) Documented the canonical header name `X-Redwood-Region` and accepted aliases (`x-redwood-region`, `Redwood-Region`) with explicit note that headers are case-insensitive but our examples use `X-Redwood-Region`. (2) Added a short “precedence” section: explicit region header > account default region (Console setting) > auto (closest healthy region) when no header is provided. (3) Added supported region value format + examples used in the report (`us-east-1`, `us-west-2`, `eu-west-1`, `ap-southeast-1`) and a note that availability can be account/tier dependent. (4) Added fallback behavior note: if a requested region is unavailable for the model/account, the request fails with 4xx by default; to allow automatic failover you must opt in via `X-Redwood-Region-Fallback: auto` (or specify a concrete fallback region), and we include the exact error payload shape. (5) Updated README + curl snippets used by Solutions/DX so they match the benchmark reproduction steps.

Why: This is intentionally a docs-only change, but it reduces confusion during the benchmark launch and prevents prospects from misconfiguring region selection when validating the report numbers.

How to test: `pnpm test` and `pnpm lint` (docs link check runs in CI). Manually verify snippets: `curl https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1" -d '{"model":"rw-llama-3-70b-instruct","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ping"}]}'`.

Notes for benchmark report cross-linking: The “How to replicate” section in the report should reference `X-Redwood-Region` and link to `/docs/openai-compat/region-selection` (added here). No product behavior changed.

Illustrative snippet (new):

Region selection headers
- `X-Redwood-Region: <region>` (recommended)
- `X-Redwood-Region-Fallback: auto | <region>` (optional)

Example:
`X-Redwood-Region: ap-southeast-1`
`X-Redwood-Region-Fallback: us-west-2`

Error when region not available (default):
HTTP 409
`{"error":{"type":"routing_error","message":"Requested region 'ap-southeast-1' is not enabled for this account/model. Remove X-Redwood-Region or enable fallback."}}`

Checklist: [x] Examples updated in README and doc page [x] Added note about account-dependent region availability [x] Link-checker passes [x] Reviewed language against external claims guidelines (no performance claims added).

docs: document fallback header + error payload for unavailable region
chore: add redirect for old /regions doc anchor

conversation:
Mina Haddad (review): The header name looks good, but please be explicit about what happens if the region is not enabled for the account. Some of our EU prospects will test `eu-west-1` vs `eu-central-1` and may not have both. Also clarify whether we ever silently reroute when a region is unhealthy.

Wei Chen (author): Good call. Added: (a) “availability is account/tier dependent” callout with pointer to Console Regions page, (b) default behavior is 409 routing_error (no silent reroute), and (c) opt-in failover via `X-Redwood-Region-Fallback`. Also added explicit wording that “auto” routing only applies when no region header is set.

Ravi Menon (review): Two nits: 1) Use one canonical header in examples (prefer `X-Redwood-Region`). 2) Mention precedence order; people will ask whether account default overrides the header.

Wei Chen (author): Updated all examples to `X-Redwood-Region` and added a short precedence list near the top.

Elliot Price (review): Please ensure the doc URL we’re linking from the benchmark report is stable. Can we add a redirect from the old anchor used in a couple drafts?

Wei Chen (author): Added a redirect in `docs/_redirects` and confirmed link-checker passes.

Mina Haddad (final): Approved.
Ravi Menon (final): Approved.

Merge: Squash merged into `main`.
release_notes: Docs only: clarified how to select regions using the OpenAI-compatible API via `X-Redwood-Region` (plus fallback options) to support benchmark report reproduction.
